_comment: STARTING ASSUMPTIONS, NOT MARITIME SAFETY RULES. These are desk-derived from Beaufort force and Douglas sea-state conventions plus common recreational practice, and are meant to be tuned against real observations and local expert feedback (see docs/thresholds.md). Every value is editable here without touching code; the version string is written into every stored report so a rating can always be traced back to the table that produced it.

units.gust_kt: knots, maximum forecast gust in the window
units.wind_kt: knots, mean sustained wind at 10 m
units.wave_m: metres, maximum combined significant wave height in the window
units.sst_c: degrees Celsius, mean sea surface temperature

gust_policy._comment: Which gust number drives a rating. Measured against live Open-Meteo data for all six sites (scripts/threshold-report.mjs, 2026-08-27): the median gust factor was 3.8x the sustained wind and the maximum 10.9x, where real-world factors are 1.3-2.0x. Rating a whole day from a single anomalous hour produced AVOID or CAUTION for sailing 94% of the time - a report that never says yes is a report people stop reading.
gust_policy._policy: 'sustained' rates on the strongest gust actually held for min_sustained_hours; 'peak' rates on the single worst hour. Either way the peak is NEVER hidden: it is shown in the report, it raises the GUST_SPIKE flag, and a peak above the caution threshold still forces at least CAUTION - so a spiky day can never be rated GOOD.

FORECAST_UNCERTAIN._comment: Ratings already use the conservative end of the ensemble, which guards against under-calling. This flag guards against over-confidence: when the models disagree this widely, even the conservative figure is unreliable, so nothing may be rated GOOD. Thresholds sit above the measured mean disagreement (0.33 m / 10.9 kt raw) so the flag marks genuinely wide splits rather than firing every day.

GUST_SPIKE._comment: A gust factor of 1.3-2.0 over the sustained wind is normal, up to ~3 in convective conditions. Above 4 for only an hour or two is usually a model artefact. The peak still drives the rating - this flag only lets the report say the peak is brief.

data_quality._comment: Essential fields gate the whole report: missing any of them forces AVOID everywhere, per the spec's 'insufficient essential data' rule. Currents and sea temperature are deliberately NOT essential - coastal marine models return them inconsistently, and treating them as essential would produce a permanently useless AVOID. Missing sea temperature instead caps swimming at CAUTION.

windows._comment: Local Africa/Algiers hours. 'day' is the headline window and spans the practical daylight activity period.
